root.name: Sicilian Defense: Acton Extension
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 g6 3. c4 Bh6

overview: Black fianchettoes with ...g6 and, instead of the usual ...Bg7, plays 3...Bh6 against the Maroczy-style 3.c4, offering to trade the dark-squared bishop for White's. White keeps the e4/c4 clamp and usually answers Nc3 and d4-style central play; Black tries to rid itself of the cramped position by trading pieces. Unfamiliar line, read from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the c4/e4 pawns and play for a Maroczy-type bind
Trade or avoid the dark-squared bishop swap and develop with Nc3, d4

black_ideas.idea: Swap the bishop on h6 or after ...Bxc1 to ease the cramp

typical_structures.structure: Maroczy bind with pawns on c4 and e4 against ...c5/...d6

character.notes: Quiet manoeuvring, no forcing sequences evident.

soundness.notes: Odd but harmless; Black is not in danger.

structure.notes: Sicilian asymmetry with half-open d-file after d4.

approach.notes: Rare sideline of the Hyperaccelerated Dragon.

level.notes: Little theory, plans are fairly clear.

character.reason: Neither forcing nor especially hard to break down.

soundness.reason: The bishop trade is odd but not losing.

structure.reason: A Sicilian with c4 and e4 and a half-open d-file.

approach.reason: A rare sideline of 2...g6 that strong players seldom pick.

level.reason: Not much theory, ordinary Maroczy plans.

plans.reason: White clamps with c4 and e4.
